title: Localization criterion for a homotopically surjective map
statement: Use the universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]; the model-category conventions used below are stated explicitly in this node. Categories are complete and cocomplete, weak equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three and retract closure, and (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations) are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system consists of mutually characterized left and right diagonal-lifting classes and factorizations of all arrows; trivial means also a weak equivalence. Cofibrant and fibrant mean that the initial and terminal maps, respectively, are cofibrations and fibrations. A cofibrant replacement is a trivial fibration $QX\to X$ with $QX$ cofibrant; a fibrant replacement is a trivial cofibration $X\to TX$ with $TX$ fibrant. Combinatorial means locally presentable with small generating sets $I,J$ whose right lifting classes are the trivial fibrations and fibrations, respectively. Locally presentable means cocomplete and generated, for some regular $\kappa$, under $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve these colimits. A Quillen adjunction is an ordinary adjunction whose left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. It is a Quillen equivalence when, for each cofibrant source object $A$ and fibrant target object $Y$, a map $LA\to Y$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $A\to RY$ is a weak equivalence. Left proper means that pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence. Write $\mathsf{sSet}$ for the simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] with the Kan model structure: cofibrations are monomorphisms; fibrations have the right lifting property against all horns $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ ($n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$), where $\Delta^n$ is the representable simplex and $\Lambda_i^n$ is the union of its faces other than the $i$th; weak equivalences induce a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all homotopy groups of geometric realizations. A simplicial model category is enriched, tensored and cotensored over $\mathsf{sSet}$, with the induced map of mapping simplicial sets for a cofibration and a fibration a Kan fibration, trivial if either arrow is trivial. For a simplicial model category $\mathcal A$, write $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}^h(A,Z)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(QA,TZ)$ for derived mapping spaces, computed with cofibrant and fibrant replacements in its original structure; equivalence of spaces means weak homotopy equivalence of these Kan complexes. For a set $S$ of arrows of $\mathcal A$, an object $Z$ is $S$-local if $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}^h(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$. A left Bousfield localization $L_S\mathcal A$ is a model structure on the same category with the same cofibrations and with weak equivalences the maps inducing equivalences of these mapping spaces into every fibrant $S$-local object. Let $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$ be a Quillen adjunction between combinatorial model categories, with $\mathcal M$ left proper and simplicial. Suppose that, for every fibrant $X$ in $\mathcal N$ and every cofibrant replacement $q:QRX\to RX$, the composite $LQRX\xrightarrow{Lq}LRX\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_X}X$ is a weak equivalence (homotopical surjectivity). Choose a functorial cofibrant-replacement functor $Q$ in $\mathcal M$. Then there is a small set $S$ of arrows of $\mathcal M$ such that $LQ(s)$ is a weak equivalence for each $s\in S$, and the same adjoint functors induce a Quillen equivalence $L_S\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N$.
